review_comments.body: blocking: Keep synthetic call keys separate from provider indexes — When an index-less call arrives before a different explicitly indexed call, `max(...)+1` can reserve that later call's real index. For example, index-less `call_b` with arguments `{}` occupies key `0`; a subsequent `call_a` with `index=0` overwrites its ID/name and appends its arguments into the same entry, producing one `call_a` with invalid arguments `{}{}` and losing `call_b`. Distinct IDs make these unambiguously different calls, so synthetic keys must not alias provider indexes. This also regresses the indexed call: the exact pre-fix control records its arguments correctly. Reproduction: reproduced — `python -m pytest posthog/test/ai/openai/test_review_1091_probes.py` fails on the reviewed head because `test_indexless_call_does_not_corrupt_later_indexed_call` observes `{}{}` instead of `{}`, while that same test passes on the merge base.

blocking: Update the public API snapshot for the widened signature — Changing this parameter to `Dict[Union[int, str], ...]` changes a signature tracked in `references/public_api_snapshot.txt:1303`, but the snapshot still declares `Dict[int, ...]`. This breaks the existing Public API snapshot CI job; regenerate and review the snapshot alongside the intentional annotation change. Reproduction: reproduced — `uv run --no-sync make public_api_check` fails on reviewed head `a0f81224` with this one-line signature mismatch, while the same check passes on merge base `1b865499`.

Fixed in 270b177f9d74cb753eb1701f37112c456355d93b. Reproduced with `uv run --no-sync make public_api_check`: it failed on the one-line accumulator annotation mismatch before regeneration and passes afterward. The regenerated snapshot has exactly that one changed line. Snapshot-script tests, all OpenAI tests (100 passed, 1 skipped), Ruff lint, and formatting also pass. This records the external contributor’s public-signature change (`Dict[int, ...]` → `Dict[Union[int, str], ...]`); no agreed issue or SDK spec defining this helper API was identified.

Verified the existing fix, now signed as 1f8e5342f2f95558b1d2a8a74978360a300c30aa (previously 8fed35a). Synthetic `no-index-N` keys cannot alias provider integer indexes. The retained `test_indexless_call_does_not_corrupt_later_indexed_call` and ordering test both pass on the current head; the complete converter file has 23 passing tests, and the OpenAI suite has 100 passed, 1 skipped. No further production-code change was necessary for this thread.

comments.body: Thanks, good catch. Fixed in 8fed35a: calls without an index now get keys of their own (`no-index-N`) instead of `max + 1`, so they can no longer take an index the provider sends later, and an argument-only delta continues the most recently added call. Added your scenario as `test_indexless_call_does_not_corrupt_later_indexed_call` (it fails on the previous head with `{}{}` and passes now) plus a test that the calls keep their arrival order. a0f8122 widens the accumulator's key type in `_streaming.py` to match.
